The warrant canary page could alert mods and users that something is afoot, and that content needs to be monitored closer than usual.

Here are some resources that can help

  • Electronic Frontier Foundation FAQ - https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2014/04/warrant-canary-faq
  • Auto Canary Generator - https://firstlook.org/code/project/autocanary/
  • Canary watch website - https://www.canarywatch.org/

I am not a lawyer, but from my limited understanding, if it' is deemed illegal to advertise that you've received a court order of some kind, it is also illegal to intentionally and knowingly take any action that has the effect of advertising the receipt of that order. This includes removing any "Warrant Canary". You would likely face the same legal consequences as simply posting something that explicitly says you've received something. If any actual lawyers have a different legal interpretation, I'd love to hear it.

Or you can go on pretending "safe spaces" like r***it and other companies who have their heads firmly planted up the asses of our "beneficial" dictators would actually remove it's canary clause if it will or has received an NSA letter. Whatever gets your goat.

Who is to know that the NSA doesn't require companies to place those canaries there in the first place? With all the secret court systems and secret laws in place it is impossible to know. Also scary is the fact that precedence would imply that claiming ignorance of these secret laws is no defense.
Apple removed theirs, for what that's worth.

I think it is better to just assume that every single US corporation and most non-US corporations have already received an NSA letter, regardless of if they still have a "Warrant Canary" or not. We will never actually know unless another Snowden-type event occurs, and I doubt the NSA will let that happen again.
